title: SLOs and honest measurement
intro: Numbers mean nothing without targets, and averages lie. Quick check.

choices: the total time for the full response
how long before the FIRST output token appears
the average gap between streamed tokens
tokens per second across all requests
questions.explanation: TTFT = time to first token — the silence before anything appears. ITL is the gap between tokens; request latency is end-to-end; throughput is the fleet-wide rate.

questions.prompt: Your dashboard shows mean latency 180 ms; p95 is 1.9 s. What's the right read?
choices: Fine — the mean is under the 200 ms target
Tail-latency trouble: 5%+ of users wait 10× longer than the average suggests
The benchmark is broken; means and percentiles can't diverge
questions.explanation: A wide mean↔p95 gap IS the finding — outliers the average hides, often your heaviest users. SLOs are written and alerted at p95/p99, never the mean.

questions.prompt: Which GuideLLM traffic pattern best imitates real users?
questions.explanation: Poisson keeps the average rate fixed with random spacing — bursty like humans. Synchronous is the clean baseline, constant is steady robots, and sweep maps the whole floor-to-ceiling curve in one run.

questions.prompt: Why should GuideLLM's dataset use `samples ≥ requests`?
choices: Fewer samples would crash the benchmark
Repeated prompts hit the prefix cache and flatter the numbers
It makes the run finish faster
questions.explanation: If prompts repeat, vLLM's prefix cache reuses their KV — you'd be benchmarking the cache, not the deployment. Unique samples keep the numbers honest.
